walkthroughs.body_html:
Forces & Newton's Laws — a core area of A-Level Maths.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Forces & Newton's Laws brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Forces & Newton's Laws.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: A 5 kg mass has resultant force 20 N. Its acceleration is:
options: 4 m/s²
100 m/s²
25 m/s²
15 m/s²

mcqs.q: On Earth, the weight of a 10 kg object (take g = 9.8) is:

options: Yes — percentage changes always cancel because they are symmetric.
3(2x + 9), by only dividing the first term by the common factor.
3(2x + 3) — take out the common factor 3.
(3x + 3)(2x + 3), by trying to factorise as a quadratic.

mcqs.q: A price increases by 20% then decreases by 20%. Is the final price the same as the original?
options: They add up to 360 degrees because they make a full turn.
Yes — percentage changes always cancel because they are symmetric.
No — the final price is 96% of the original (a 4% net decrease), because each percentage is applied to a different base.
Yes — a 20% rise and a 20% fall cancel out exactly.

mcqs.q: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. What is the relationship between co-interior (allied) angles?
options: They add up to 360 degrees because they make a full turn.
Yes — percentage changes always cancel because they are symmetric.
They add up to 180 degrees.
They are equal to each other, like alternate angles.

sequence.def: Law 1 (1687): a body stays at rest or constant velocity unless forced.
Law 2: F=ma — net force gives acceleration.
Law 3: every action has an equal and opposite reaction.
Weight W=mg — a specific force acting on mass.
A resistive contact force opposing motion.
Splitting forces into components — the technique to apply all laws.
